# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: before the first management review, or when a series of numbers
  gets put forward that nobody can do anything with
- Audience: `management`
- Length: 15 minutes
- What the listeners already know: that a management system is running and that
  something gets put to them regularly

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. The deck for the practitioners sits beside it and
answers a different question: this one asks which measures should be put
forward at all, that one shows how one gets built.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

ISO/IEC 27004 answers how you tell that a management system works, and
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requires that in 9.1.

## Why it concerns the leadership

- The numbers get put to it in the management review, and it decides out of
  them
- A number with no threshold set beforehand triggers nothing and gets
  interpreted anew in every meeting
- Anyone deciding nothing gets the same number next time
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.3

# What a measure carries

## Three levels, and the third is usually missing

- What gets counted directly, and where it arises
- What gets calculated from that
- What gets read off it, together with the threshold above which something
  happens

The third level is where a measure turns into a decision. Without it, it is an
observation.

## What it does not carry

- No statement about whether the organisation meets a requirement; an audit
  decides that
- No forecast; a measure observes, a risk evaluation estimates
- No replacement for the finding of an internal audit

# How to recognise a paper that achieves nothing

## Three signs

- The share stands there and the base does not: three out of four is 75 per
  cent, thirty out of forty is too, and the two are not worth the same
- One value stands there and no series; only the second value says whether
  anything is moving
- The threshold was fixed after the collection, or not at all

## The question that exposes it

What happens if this number is worse next quarter? Where no answer comes, the
measure carries nothing and costs work all the same.

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The paper

- How many measures get put to the leadership, and which
- Who sets the threshold per measure, and when
- On what beat does the putting forward happen
- What happens to a measure that has triggered nothing in four quarters

Fewer measures with a threshold are worth more than many without. The decision
about the number is the real decision on this slide.
